When you use a command, the user will respond with "Response: " followed by the output of the commmand. Use this output to help the user complete their request.

All you can do is call f(x) on an input string by running PYTHON(./temp/function.py string). 
Try to describe the function implemented by f(x) by running experiments on it. 
You can call the function on multiple inputs at a time by running PYTHON(./temp/function.py string1 string2 string3 ...). 
We encourage testing a large range of inputs before writing a description.
The goal is to find a good simple description of f(x) that explains most of the function behavior. f(x) may combine multiple different operations.
Your description of the function should be in the following form.
[DESCRIPTION]: Describe what the function is doing in language. 
[CODE]: Write python code that approximates the behavior of the function.

Let me test more systematically to understand patterns.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py a aa aaa aaaa aaaaa ab abc abcd abcde abcdef abcdefg abcdefgh)

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py A AA AAA B BB BBB aA Aa ab AB ba BA)

Let me test strings with various lengths and characters more carefully.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "xy" "xyz" "xyzw" "xyzab" "xyzabc" "1" "12" "123" "1234" "!" "!!" "!!!" "a!" "!a")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "hello" "Hello" "HELLO" "hello!" " hello" "hello " "h e l l o")

Let me look at longer and mixed content.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "abcdefghij" "abcdefghijk" "0123456789" "The quick brown fox" "test123" "a1!B2@c3")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "x" "y" "z" "9" "0" "_" "-" "." "," "@" "#" "$")

Let me examine what might be happening with single characters versus longer strings.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "q" "w" "e" "r" "t" "y" "1" "2" "3" "4" "#" "&" "*" "(")

Let me test strings that are all the same character vs mixed, at various lengths.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "zz" "zzz" "zzzz" "zzzzz" "zzzzzz" "abab" "ababab" "aaabbb")

Let me test whether it's related to reversing, case, or something else.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "abcdef" "fedcba" "aceg" "bdfh" "1357" "2468")

Let me test spaces and how they affect output at various positions.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "a" "ab" "abc" "abcd" "abcde" "a b" "ab c" "a bc" " abc")

Let me carefully check the outputs for a clear pattern with capital letters and digits.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "Abc" "aBc" "abC" "ABC" "abc" "1bc" "a2c" "ab3" "Ab1" "aB2")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "aa" "bb" "cc" "ab" "ac" "ba" "ca" "abc" "cba" "acb")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "hello world this is a test" "a b c d e f g h")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "a" "aa" "aaa" "aaaa" "b" "bb" "bbb" "ab" "ba" "aab" "aba" "baa")

Let me try to see if output looks like a number/count related to length.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "11111" "22222" "!@#$%" "abcde" "vwxyz" "54321")

Let me test with numbers embedded to see if digits are counted or transformed.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "1" "11" "111" "1111" "a1" "1a" "a1a" "a1a1")

Let me check single character vs multiple characters more precisely.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "m" "mn" "mno" "mnop" "mnopq")

Based on all these tests, let me verify a hypothesis about whether it reverses, filters, or transforms.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "abc" "cba" "Abc" "aBc" "abc " " abc" "a-b" "a_b")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "abc" "bcd" "ABCDEF" "abcdef" "aaa bbb" "aaabbb")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "A" "B" "Z" "a" "b" "z" "0" "1" "9" " ")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "abcde" "edcba" "12345" "54321" "a1b2c3" "c3b2a1")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" "zyxwvutsrqponmlkjihgfedcba")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "abcxyz" "zyxcba" "abcdef123456" "654321fedcba")

The function appears to be an identity-like function that returns the input string as-is for typical inputs, while possibly applying a normalization step (such as lowercasing or stripping) on edge cases.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "abc" "xyz" "hello")
